Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence, present only when the answering module has one to give. It may be a sentence rendered in the request language or a language-neutral token such as "forbidden", so clients must not parse it.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

get.description: One long-lived connection, scoped by the request's tenant and the caller's effective account (the impersonated account while impersonation is in force). The server writes a frame each time the inbox gains a row for that pair, and the connection ends when the client disconnects, the entry point drains or the process stops. Every frame is named message and its data is a JSON object carrying the published event payload (message_id, tenant_id, recipient_user_id, type_key); a client reads the inbox by message_id to obtain content. Delivery is best-effort: the hub is in memory and per replica, nothing is replayed, arrival order carries no business meaning, and a connection with 64 frames already pending drops its own further frames rather than delaying the publisher. The route does not decide who may connect; host authorization does.

200.description: One text/event-stream for the life of the connection; each event is named message and its data is the published event payload as JSON. The raw event-stream body is a sequence of SSE frames, each one an event: message line, a data: line holding a JSON object, and a blank line, with no terminating frame or sentinel.

Cache-Control.description: Always no-store: an event stream must not be cached.

401.description: The request carries no identity, so there is no recipient to scope the connection to

500.description: The response writer cannot flush a stream

get.summary: Subscribe to the caller's in-app notifications as a server-sent event stream
